article.dek: The final injury report is in for Thursday night — Washington loses its starting center, the Giants are nearly clean — and the line has not moved all day.

items.headline: Lead: final designations are in — Patrick is out, Burks is expected to play, Giants nearly clean
paragraphs: The last unknowns for Thursday night are answered. Washington ruled out center Lucas Patrick with a concussion on Wednesday's final injury report, and tight end Colson Yankoff is out too with a knee injury. Nick Allegretti starts at center in Patrick's place — head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that on Tuesday, and Allegretti is the man in the middle against the Giants' pass rush on a short week.

The good news for Washington is the receiver. Treylon Burks missed Wednesday's practice with the foot injury that kept him out against the Rams, but he got no game designation at all. Quinn said the day off was planned after Burks got work on Tuesday, and the receiver is expected to be ready Thursday. His place on the active list is confirmed with the inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff.

The Giants are nearly clean. Only outside linebacker Malik Harrison carries a designation — questionable with a groin injury after being limited all week. Abdul Carter practiced in full on Wednesday after two limited days and has no designation, and neither do J.J. McCarthy or Cam Skattebo. Colton Hood, the rookie corner who was limited Tuesday, has no designation either. On a short week, that is about as healthy as a team gets.
items.takeaway: Patrick is out and Allegretti starts at center for Washington, Burks is expected to play despite missing Wednesday's practice, and the Giants' only designation is Harrison as questionable.

items.headline: Injuries: Darnold ruled out again, Willis to injured reserve, Mahomes practices in full
paragraphs: The rest of the week's quarterback news landed Wednesday. Sam Darnold is ruled out again for Seattle — ribs and quad — and he did not practice Wednesday. Drew Lock was limited with elbow and quad injuries, but he starts Sunday against the Raiders, his second straight start. Head coach Mike Macdonald said Lock is making progress and the team will keep managing his throwing workload through the week.

In Miami, the Dolphins put quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve with a groin injury, so Kyle McCord gets his first chance to lead an NFL team on Sunday against the Colts. And in Kansas City, the worry was smaller than it looked: Patrick Mahomes was a full participant in Wednesday's practice despite the knee and elbow issues that had him listed day-to-day, and Andy Reid expects him to play Sunday against the Falcons. Travis Kelce practiced in full too.

None of these games is Thursday, so none of it changes tomorrow night. But the board is still behind on all of it — it lists Darnold as Seattle's starter and Murray as Minnesota's — so if you are looking at a Sunday price, remember the board has not caught up yet.
items.takeaway: Darnold is out and Lock starts again Sunday, McCord starts for Miami with Willis on injured reserve, and Mahomes practiced in full — the board still lists Darnold and Murray as starters, so it has not caught up.

items.headline: Weather: Thursday night at MetLife is still rain, low around 40, gusts to 23 mph
paragraphs: The final forecast is in and it barely moved from this morning. The National Weather Service calls for showers Thursday, mainly after 10 a.m., with a 100% chance of precipitation and a high near 60. Thursday night brings rain, a low around 40, and a north wind at 10 to 13 mph with gusts as high as 23 mph. The chance of rain Thursday night is 80%.

Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, outdoors, so the game will be played in rain with temperatures falling toward 40 and the wind gusting into the low 20s. That is a forecast fact, not a totals edge. Rain does not pick a side or a total on its own — it is worth knowing because Thursday is outdoors and the forecast is now final, not a two-days-out guess.
items.takeaway: Rain is forecast at MetLife on Thursday night — 80% chance, low around 40, wind gusting to 23 mph. A forecast fact, not a totals edge.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — Thursday still goes through Check
paragraphs: I checked the board tonight, after the evening refresh. It is the same board as this morning — generated November 2, still showing Week 8. I re-fetched it twice and got the same file both times. The app's own freshness field says FRESH, but the timestamp says November 2. The headline cards are from the Bears-Seahawks game: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. Those games are done. Do not bet those cards.

Here is how to read them anyway, because the same three cards will be back when the board flips. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. The Seahawks moneyline is the example: the app gave Seattle a 60.0% chance to win, while the -175 price needs 63.6% to break even, so the expected value is negative. That is the point — Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. Balanced is the middle ground, a strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the app's plus-EV play — the Bears +3, with the app at 52.4% against a market that priced Chicago at 50.5%, for a small positive edge.

The board has not picked up this week's news either. It still lists Kyler Murray as Minnesota's expected starter — he is now likely out 3-4 weeks with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, and Carson Wentz started Monday night. It still lists Sam Darnold as Seattle's starter, though Darnold is ruled out and Drew Lock starts Sunday. It knows nothing about McCarthy, and there is no Commanders-Giants game on it at all. Until the board flips to Week 10, there is no card to read for Thursday, so use Check. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price for Commanders-Giants — the Giants are -2.5 at DraftKings and -1.5 at FanDuel, with the total at 41.5 — and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override. Thursday game? Thursday check.
items.takeaway: The board is still the November 2 board, nine days old, and it still shows last week's Week 8 cards — it still lists Murray and Darnold as starters and knows nothing about McCarthy — so Thursday's Commanders-Giants price goes through Check.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: the hook — the half point that decides your bet
paragraphs: The hook is the half point on a spread. A line of -2.5 has a hook. A line of -1.5 has a hook too. The hook is there so the bet cannot push — somebody wins, somebody loses, no ties. But it does more than that: it decides whole games.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say your team is a 2.5-point favorite and wins by exactly 2. You lose. The same team, the same game, at -1.5 — you win. Nothing about the football changed. The price did. That is why a half point is worth real money, and why bettors shop for it: one book has -2.5, another has -1.5, and the second book is giving you a better bet on the same team.

Now watch for it in real life: when two books list the same team a half point apart, the shorter spread is the better price on the same team. A two-point win cashes -1.5 and loses -2.5. That is the hook doing its work — and it is why shopping the number is worth the minute it takes.
items.takeaway: The hook is the half point on a spread — it decides bets on the exact same game, so a -1.5 is a genuinely better price than a -2.5, and shopping for it is worth the minute it takes.

items.headline: Thursday's line did not move all day — Giants -2.5, total 41.5, and a better number is sitting at FanDuel
paragraphs: Nothing moved on the spread or the total today. The Giants are still -2.5 at DraftKings, the total is still 41.5, and those are the same numbers as this morning. The only drift was on the moneyline: the Giants went from about -135 this morning to -142 now, with the Commanders at +120. A small move, in New York's direction.

The move that matters already happened, and it happened on the news. The Giants opened as 1.5-point home favorites and are now -2.5. The total opened at 44.5 and is now 41.5 — down three points. The spread moved a point once the McCarthy news firmed up, and the total fell as the rain forecast firmed up. The money is with the move, not against it: reported DraftKings splits from Monday evening had 71% of spread tickets and 89% of the money on the Giants. Tickets and handle agree on New York, so this is not a public-vs-money split — it is a popular side that the money likes too. That is why there is no Fade tonight.

Here is the number worth knowing before kickoff: FanDuel has the Giants at -1.5 (-120), a full point better than DraftKings' -2.5. A two-point Giants win cashes -1.5 and loses -2.5. If your book has a Thursday number you like — especially a -1.5 — run it through Check and let the app judge your price. The app board has caught none of this. It still shows Week 8 prices from November 2, and there is no Commanders-Giants game on it at all.
items.takeaway: Giants -2.5 and total 41.5 held all day after moving a point and three points since opening — the money agrees with the tickets on New York, so there is no Fade, and FanDuel's -1.5 is a full point better than DraftKings' -2.5.

items.headline: Thursday is tomorrow — if your book has -1.5, run Check tonight
paragraphs: Everything that could be answered before kickoff is answered. McCarthy is confirmed, the final designations are in, and the forecast is final. The only thing left to wait for is the inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff on Thursday, and that only matters if your bet needs a specific name in the lineup. If it does not, there is nothing left to wait for.

So run Check tonight. The line has already moved once this week — the Giants went from -1.5 to -2.5 while people waited — and FanDuel still has a -1.5 sitting there. If your book has a Thursday number you like and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number tomorrow, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too. And if your book's number is worse than the one you want, Check still tells you — a no-bet verdict on a bad price is the app doing its job.

One last thing: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. That is price mechanics, not a stake. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and how aggressive you want to be — let it do that part.
items.takeaway: The final designations and the forecast are in, so the only wait left is the inactives about 90 minutes before Thursday's kickoff — if your book has a number you like and Check says bet, bet it now.
